content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Managing Resource Constraints in Docker (CPU, Memory, IO)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, a Docker container has no resource constraints and can use as much CPU, memory, and IO as the host kernel allows. In production environments, this can lead to 'noisy neighbor' issues where a single runaway container starves other applications. This tutorial covers how to enforce strict resource limits on Docker containers to ensure system stability."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Memory Constraints"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Docker allows you to limit the maximum amount of RAM a container can use, as well as the swap space. If a container reaches its memory limit, the Linux kernel invokes the Out-Of-Memory (OOM) killer, which typically terminates the container process."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-m or --memory: Sets the maximum memory limit (e.g., 512m, 2g)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"--memory-swap: Sets the total memory and swap limit combined."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"docker run -d --name memory-limited-container -m 512m --memory-swap 1g nginx"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. CPU Constraints"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"CPU limits dictate how much processing power a container can consume relative to other containers on the host. You can allocate CPU shares, restrict containers to specific cores, or limit CPU periods."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"--cpu-shares: Specifies a relative weight (default is 1024) compared to other containers."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"--cpus: Specifies the exact number of CPUs the container can use (e.g., 1.5 means one and a half cores)."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"--cpuset-cpus: Restricts execution to specific CPU cores (e.g., 0-3 or 1,3)."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"docker run -d --name cpu-limited-container --cpus=\"1.5\" --cpuset-cpus=\"0,1\" nginx"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Block IO Constraints"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Block Input/Output (Blkio) limits throttle read and write operations on storage devices. While you can limit IOPS (Input/Output Operations Per Second) and bandwidth, these flags apply primarily to direct IO operations."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"--device-read-bps: Limit read rate (bytes per second) for a specific device."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"--device-write-bps: Limit write rate (bytes per second) for a specific device."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"docker run -d --name io-limited-container --device-read-bps /dev/sda:10mb --device-write-bps /dev/sda:5mb nginx"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Monitoring Resource Usage"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"To verify that your resource constraints are working properly and to monitor live usage statistics for all running containers, use the built-in docker stats command."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"docker stats"}]
